body: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so this SMS cron deletes *every* WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever the method. Right now only this handler increments retryCount. But once the email or WhatsApp crons start using the new column (or someone sets it another way), this job will silently delete their reminders too. Scope it with `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, or move `method` outside the OR.

`twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when the user or team is locked for SMS sending (`isLockedForSMSSending`). That is an admin/temporary state, not a bad phone number. With this change, a locked account's reminders get their retryCount bumped on each cron run and are deleted after two runs, so after the lock is lifted those reminders are gone for good. Only count real delivery/validation failures as retries, e.g. have scheduleSMS tell 'locked' apart from 'failed', or skip the increment when it returns undefined because of the lock.

Every exception now counts as a retry. That includes transient ones: `checkSMSRateLimit` throwing on the monthly rate limit, Twilio 5xx/network errors, and errors from template building or the `prisma.profile.findFirst` call. Two cron runs hitting a rate-limit window or a Twilio outage will permanently delete valid reminders. The PR is meant to stop retrying permanently invalid numbers, so consider only incrementing for non-retryable Twilio errors (e.g. invalid 'To' number codes such as 21211/21614), not for every error.

This `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block isn't guarded. If it throws, the error escapes the `for` loop and the handler rejects, so none of the remaining reminders get processed in this run. It can throw because of a DB error, or P2025 if the reminder was deleted at the same moment, e.g. by a booking cancellation. Wrap it in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`/`increment` so a missing row doesn't throw.

Suppose the Twilio schedule call succeeds but the following `update` (line 169, setting `scheduled: true`/`referenceId`) throws. The catch block then bumps retryCount. The SMS is already queued at Twilio, but the row keeps `scheduled: false` and no referenceId. The next run schedules a duplicate SMS, and once retryCount > 1 the row is deleted. After that, cancelling or rescheduling the booking can't cancel the queued Twilio messages, since there's no referenceId. Handle the post-schedule DB failure separately rather than counting it as a scheduling failure. Also prefer `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` over `reminder.retryCount + 1` so a stale read can't overwrite a concurrent update.
